newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso holds gains at close in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso holds gains at close in quiet trade.

text.p: The Mexican peso held on to early firmness at the close on Friday as foreign investors stepped in to the Mexican markets, during what traders said was a session made quiet by the approaching holiday season.
"I think some one has been dumping long (dollar) positions, combined with those going short into the weekend and foreigners switching into pesos," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart stood 1.8 and 0.9 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.8400/7.8450 and 7.8370/7.8400 per dollar.
Same-day contracts had closed earlier 2.45 centavos firmer at 7.8220/7.8250 per dollar.
Most traders forecast the 48-hour peso closing the year at 7.85 per dollar, but some urged caution over inflation data for the first half of December, due out on Monday.

"I feel the market doesn't wish to do very much over the weeks to come, but if inflation and trade balance figures are wide of expectations we could see an unfavorable start to the new year," a dealer said.
The 48-hour peso closed the week 6.6 centavos firmer than last week. Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.83/7.88 for next week.
